rows.measured: Cytochrome c oxidase from the sulfide-spring Puyacatengo and Pichucalco populations keeps significant activity across hydrogen sulfide concentrations of 0 to 0.9 micromolar, where the enzyme from neighbouring non-sulfidic populations loses activity; isolated liver mitochondria from sulfidic fish hold maximal respiration and spare respiratory capacity higher than non-sulfidic fish across 0 to 90 micromolar hydrogen sulfide. Numbers read from the Methods and Results of the full text today.
rows.cite: Greenway, Ryan, et al. "Convergent evolution of conserved mitochondrial pathways underlies repeated adaptation to extreme environments." *Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America* 117, no. 28 (2020): 16424-16430. https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2004223117 PMID 32586956.
rows.origins: Three independent colonisations of sulfide springs within the Poecilia mexicana complex, confirmed from 13,390,303 genome-wide SNPs; on a wider scale, 10 independent sulfide-spring lineages across five genera of Poeciliidae spanning over 40 million years, with convergent amino acid substitutions at six codons in one cytochrome oxidase subunit and two in another. Same paper: Greenway, Ryan, et al. "Convergent evolution of conserved mitochondrial pathways underlies repeated adaptation to extreme environments." *Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America* 117, no. 28 (2020): 16424-16430. https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2004223117 PMID 32586956. "Evolution in extreme environments: replicated phenotypic differentiation in livebearing fish inhabiting sulfidic springs." *Evolution* 65, no. 8 (2011): 2213-28. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1558-5646.2011.01298.x PMID 21790570.
